label: Medical practice
recognise: Clinics, GP and family practices, dentists, specialists, physiotherapy, diagnostic labs, pharmacies and other healthcare providers.
research: What websites of similar practices (same specialty and, if given, the same area) usually show, and what patients look for before they book.

pages.title: Home
pages.purpose: Who the practice is, the main services, how to book, opening hours and location.

pages.title: About us
pages.purpose: The practice's story, its approach to care and what patients can expect.

pages.title: Services
pages.purpose: Each treatment or service in plain words: who it's for and how to get it.

pages.title: Our doctors
pages.purpose: The clinicians with their roles, qualifications and areas of care.

pages.title: Appointments
pages.purpose: How to book, what to bring, cancellation and first-visit information.

pages.title: Contact
pages.purpose: Phone, address, map directions, opening hours and the emergency notice.

pages.title: Privacy policy
pages.purpose: How patient information sent through the site is collected, used and protected.

sections.header: The practice's name or logo, the main pages, and a prominent Book an appointment button (phone number on small screens).
sections.footer: Address, phone, opening hours, the emergency notice, quick links and the privacy policy.
sections.homepage: A calm, trustworthy hero with what the practice offers and a booking button; the main services; why patients choose it; the doctors; opening hours and location; a final call to book.

rules: Never promise outcomes or cures, and don't make medical claims the owner didn't give.
Say clearly that the site is not for emergencies, with the local emergency number where the owner gives it.
Use plain, reassuring language a worried patient understands; explain medical terms.
Qualifications, registrations and prices only as the owner gives them.
A calm, clean look: plenty of white space, soft colours, readable type, high contrast.

demo.note: Where the owner gave no details, write these as clearly marked samples for them to replace.

questions.title: What care do you offer?
questions.lead: The services patients come for most, first.
questions.why: The Services page and the homepage lead with them.

questions.title: Where and when can patients find you?
questions.lead: These go in your site details, the footer and the Contact page.
questions.why: Only you know your address, phone and opening hours.

questions.title: How do patients book?
questions.lead: This sets the button in your header.
questions.why: It sets the button in your header.

questions.title: Should the site show your doctors?
questions.lead: Patients like to know who they'll see.
questions.why: The Our doctors page needs them.

questions.title: What should it look and feel like?
questions.lead: The feel sets the colours; your logo and photos make it yours.
questions.why: Your logo and photos make the site yours.

fields.label: Photos (up to 6)
fields.hint: Your practice, your team, your rooms.

questions.title: What should the emergency notice say?
questions.lead: Every page says the site isn't for emergencies.
questions.why: Medical sites must say where to go in an emergency.
